item.title: VARCHAR Versus NVARCHAR in SQL: Which Character Data Type Should You Select
item.description:
“VARCHAR Versus NVARCHAR in SQL: Which Character Data Type Should You Select”

When structuring tables in database systems, particularly SQL Server, the choice between VARCHAR and NVARCHAR for storing character strings is a pivotal design decision. This selection impacts storage efficiency, handling of international characters, indexing limitations, and overall query performance due to character encoding conversions. What are the distinct characteristics of each type, and what considerations should drive the final choice for modern application development?

item.title: Decimal Versus Float Data Types in SQL: Choosing Precision for Data Integrity
item.description:
“Decimal Versus Float Data Types in SQL: Choosing Precision for Data Integrity”

When architecting database schemas, selecting the appropriate numeric data type is paramount for data integrity and application performance. Specifically, how should a developer choose between the Exact Numeric Types (DECIMAL, NUMERIC, MONEY, SMALLMONEY) and the Approximate Numeric Types (FLOAT, REAL)?

What are the fundamental distinctions regarding value representation, precision limits, performance characteristics, and suitable use cases for these types in a system like SQL Server?
